findings.current: “Yes, my lord. Did you not know?”
findings.defect: The translation omits the contrast that a typical subordinate would deny having grievances, while Wipeng is one of the few people who can openly give Jin Wikyung grief. That contrast explains the bluntness of his reply.
findings.rationale: The Korean explicitly gives the expected denial and contrasts it with Wipeng’s unusual freedom to rebuke Jin Wikyung; the assembled English leaves out that explanation.
findings.replacement: In an ordinary lord-and-subject relationship, he would have said, “Oh, no, not at all.” But Wipeng was one of the few people who could openly lay into Jin Wikyung. “Yes, a great deal. Did you not know?”

findings.current: “An… an imugi’s claw? Is it real?”
findings.defect: The source describes suspicion and astonishment mingling in Jang Taebo’s eyes as he looks at the unfamiliar material. That reaction is omitted before his question.
findings.rationale: The Korean explicitly describes both the uncertainty that the claw could be real and his shock at seeing an unfamiliar substance; the English keeps the question but drops the visual reaction.
findings.replacement: As Jang Taebo stared at the imugi’s claw, suspicion and astonishment at the unfamiliar material mingled in his eyes. “An… an imugi’s claw? Is it real?”

summary: The translation is largely faithful, but it omits a character beat about Wipeng’s unusual candor and a reaction to the imugi’s claw; it also blurs a specific reference to secret techniques.
